status: Laid on table 2026-03-11; substance moved via companion CS/CS/SB 484, which was enacted as Ch. 2026-65
key_provisions: House companion to SB 484. Current official summary included NDA limits, local planning authority, construction-permit study requirements for certain data centers, PSC large-load tariff rules, water-permit limits, and reclaimed-water provisions.

sponsors: Sen. Bryan Avila; co-introducers Sen. Clay Yarborough and Sen. Don Gaetz
status: Approved by Governor 2026-05-07; Chapter No. 2026-65, effective 2026-07-01
key_provisions: Preserves local comprehensive planning and land development authority for large load customers; says large load customers are not electric substations for local siting purposes; creates PSC large-load tariff requirements for 50 MW or larger customers; bars cost shifting to general ratepayers; allows curtailment for grid stability; creates large-scale data center water-permit requirements; requires hearings for certain consumptive use applications; authorizes reclaimed-water requirements; directs OPPAGA study.

status: Died on Calendar 2026-03-13 (companion bill provisions passed via CS/CS/SB 484, Ch. 2026-65)
key_provisions: Would have created a public-records exemption for information about a person's plans, intentions, or interest in locating a data center, with future repeal review and public-necessity language.

Would have required approval applications and existing data centers to disclose specified information; required DEP to post information; added penalties; and limited certain tax benefits or protections for noncompliance.

sponsors: House Ways and Means Committee; Rep. Wyman Duggan and co-introducers
status: Approved by Governor 2025-06-30 (with line-item veto of certain appropriation provisions); Chapter 2025-208
key_provisions: Revised Florida's data center tax framework, including data center eligibility threshold changes captured in prior research.

sponsors: House Ways and Means Committee; Rep. Jim Boyd and co-introducers
key_provisions: Created Florida's data center sales and use tax exemption framework, including investment and critical IT load criteria captured in prior research.

status: Passed House 2024-03-01 (Third Reading); passed Senate Second Reading as amended (SD1) and referred to WAM 2024-03-20; no further action recorded - died at the end of the 2023-2024 biennium without passing the Senate
key_provisions: Earlier House version of the data-server tax-credit reinstatement proposal.

sponsors: Same House sponsor group as HR196
status: House adopted 2026-04-09; transmitted to Senate; Senate adopted as amended (SD1) 2026-04-27; returned to and adopted in final form by the House same day - fully adopted by both chambers
key_provisions: Concurrent-resolution version of the large-data-center working group request. The HD1 text uses the same 5 MW threshold and study scope as HR196.

sponsors: Reps. Nicole Lowen, Terez Amato, Della Au Belatti, Tina Grandinetti, Jeanne Kapela, Sue Keohokapu-Lee Loy, Matthias Kusch, Lisa Marten, Tyson Miyake, Amy Perruso, Mahina Poepoe, Shirley Ann Templo, Chris Todd
status: Adopted by the House in final form 2026-04-09 (House-only resolution; no Senate action required)
key_provisions: Requests the Hawaii State Energy Office to convene a working group to study data centers requiring 5 MW or more in instantaneous demand. Topics include utility impacts, ratepayer protection, water use, greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy alignment, and grid reliability.

sponsors: Sens. Sharon Moriwaki, Henry Aquino, Stanley Chang, Kurt Fevella, Troy Hashimoto, Maile Shimabukuro, Michelle Kidani
party: Mixed D/R (Fevella was the Senate's only Republican; remaining co-sponsors are Democrats)
status: Passed Senate 2024-03-05 (received in House); passed House Second Reading as amended (HD1) and referred to FIN 2024-03-20; no further action recorded - died at the end of the 2023-2024 biennium without passing the House
key_provisions: Senate companion to HB1784; would have reinstated the technology infrastructure renovation tax credit and included data servers.

sponsors: Sens. Donovan Dela Cruz, Henry Aquino, Stanley Chang, Lorraine Inouye, Dru Kanuha, Sharon Moriwaki, Michelle Kidani
party: D (all listed co-sponsors are Hawaii Democrats)
status: Passed Senate 2023 (SD2); passed House Second Reading as amended (HD1) and referred to FIN 2023-03-24; carried over to 2024 Regular Session (housekeeping entry 2023-12-11); no further action recorded during 2024 - died at the end of the 2023-2024 biennium without passing the House
key_provisions: State-government IT bill that would have decommissioned or relocated the OETS Kalanimoku data center and set state cloud/storage and procurement requirements.

sponsors: Sens. Henry Aquino, Stanley Chang, Kurt Fevella, Carol Fukunaga
status: Passed Senate 2025; passed House Second Reading as amended (HD1) and referred to FIN 2025-03-21; carried over to 2026 Regular Session (housekeeping entry 2025-12-08); no further action recorded during the 2026 session - died in House FIN at the end of the 2025-2026 biennium without passing the House
key_provisions: Would temporarily reinstate the technology infrastructure renovation tax credit for taxable years beginning after 2025-12-31 and expand "technology-enabled infrastructure" to include data servers. Not a moratorium bill.

sponsors: Sen. Glenn Wakai and Senate co-sponsors including Angus McKelvey, Brandon Elefante, Carol Fukunaga, Tim Richards, Jarrett Keohokalole, Joy San Buenaventura, Karl Rhoads, and Stanley Chang
party: D (all listed Senate co-sponsors caucus as Democrats; Hawaii Senate has had no Republican members since 2024)
status: SR90 (Senate-only resolution): adopted by the Senate as amended (SD1) 2026-04-09, certified copies sent 2026-05-12 - final action, fully adopted. SCR95 (companion Senate Concurrent Resolution): passed Senate as amended (SD1) 2026-04-09, transmitted to and received by the House the same day, referred to House EEP/FIN 2026-04-10; no further House action recorded - died in House committee, never adopted by the second chamber
key_provisions: Senate measures requesting a Hawaii State Energy Office working group on large data centers, including possible reporting, water-impact assessment, and safeguards for ratepayers and grid reliability.
